newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher, await crop damage numbers.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher, await crop damage numbers.

text.p: FCOJ futures continued to rack up gains on last weekend's freeze in Florida, as growers assessed damage and began to quantify losses, traders said.
The most-active March contract closed up 0.20 to 86.85 cents, traded 88.40 to 86.80 cents. The back months settled 1.55 higher to 0.05 lower.
A reliable estimate of losses to Florida's citrus crop remains several days away, however, said the growers' organization, Florida Citrus Mutual.
Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with PaineWebber, predicts about 10 percent of the crop suffered freeze damage, based on the market's reaction.
Ultimately, prices could reach new lows, he said, citing a record U.S. crop, a possible record Brazilian crop, and a strong U.S. dollar, which could limit sales to Europe and possibly Japan.
In the near term, prices could stage another rally and then recede, analysts said. Major resistance was pegged between 89.80 to 90.30 in March, with nearby resistance seen at 88.00.
Support was put at the recent low of 84.00 cents, and then between 83.00 to 82.50 cents.
